item.title: [SwiftHFR] Reader: links take an accent-derived colour that reaches 4.5:1 (#1374)
item.body:
Closes #1374
Claim: mac/mac-mbp
Author model: Sonnet 5.5 (mac/mac-mbp-w1374)

### Problem
Body links are drawn in `--action`, the accent (fill colour: S 0.65 / B 1 by day). As text it is 1.52:1 on white at the default hue, 1.07 at 60 degrees, 2.24 in dark at 240 degrees.

### Cause
`a { color: var(--action) }` in `reader.css` reuses the accent for text; the accent was designed for fills and the app tint.

### Change
- `ThemeAppearance+LinkColor.swift` (pure, Swift): `linkColor(dark:)` moves the accent toward black (light) or white (dark) by the smallest share that reaches 4.7:1 (4.5 plus margin for CSS-composited tints) on every link surface (page, placeholder, `--love`, `--modo`, quotes nested to about 15 % text, 15 % accent tint), and also after a continuation's 75 % opacity fade. An accent that already passes is untouched. Sent as `--app-link-light` / `--app-link-dark` (Legacy only).
- `reader.css`: `--link` defaults to those variables (fallback `--action`); `a` and `[code]` blue keyword spans (`span[style="color:blue"]`, the other accent-coloured text) use it. Underline and weight unchanged. The accent still paints fills, controls and the app tint.
- Gallery themes: unchanged, they send no link variable and keep their own `link` token (already held to 4.5:1 on their surfaces by `ThemeDefinition`'s contrast checks).
- Legacy look decision (for the operator): legacy draws body links and the `[code]` keyword in the accent too (`style-liste-light.css:339-341` `.message .content .right a { color: var(--color-action) }`, `:631-633` `.olcode .span`, `--color-action` = `ThemeColors.tintColor`, `MessagesView.swift:2833,2841`, `ThemeColors.m:618-619`, @ `87fe0d1c`), so this deliberately changes a legacy behaviour (1.5:1 at the default hue). The hue stays recognisable (test: within 6 degrees), only lightness moves; at the default hue the light link is a dark teal. Ledger below.

### Before / after (WKWebView, `ReaderLinkContrastWebTests`, page link, Blanc / standard dark)
| Hue | Mode | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| 190 (default) | light | 1.52 | >= 4.5 (test) |
| 60 | light | 1.07 | >= 4.5 |
| 240 | dark | 2.24 | >= 4.5 |
| every 30 degrees + 190 | light Blanc/Doux, dark standard/darker/oled at 150 %, modern + classic | red: 2490 issues | all pass |

Surfaces per run: page, quote, own quote, allowlisted quote, nested quotes (2 levels), spoiler, code keyword span, on plain, allowlisted, moderation and own messages; continuation too (hues 190/60/240).

### Tests
- New `ReaderLinkContrastWebTests` (hosted, real WKWebView, rendered colours via the shared `ContrastProbe`): red first against the old CSS (2490 issues, continuation failing at 3.0-3.6), green after. Pure tests: hue kept, readable accent kept, Legacy sends the variables and a theme none.
- Updated variable counts (+2) in `ThemeAppearanceTests` and `ThemeLightStyleTests`.
- Also green: `ReaderContrastAccentAndNestingWebTests`, `ReaderAllowlistContrastWebTests`, `ThemeEngineTests`, `SeasonalGalleryThemeTests`, `VisibilityWebTests`, `ReaderPlusButtonWebTests`. Full suite left to CI.
- `pre-commit run --all-files` passes.
- SwiftLint by hand: line_length 140, file_length 400 (ThemeAppearance.swift 360), type/function body length, cyclomatic complexity, function_parameter_count (<= 5, a `Run` struct carries the measure), large_tuple, vertical_whitespace, trailing_comma, inclusive_language, multiple_closures_with_trailing_closure, identifier_name.

### Ledger

```changelog
| UX | Lecteur : les liens et les mots-clés de code d'un message prennent une couleur dérivée de l'accent, assombrie (thème clair) ou éclaircie (thème sombre) jusqu'à 4,5:1 ; avec l'accent par défaut, ils étaient à 1,5:1 sur fond blanc. | #1374 | `style-liste-light.css:339-341, 631-633` @ `87fe0d1c` |
```

```gap-new
Section: Reader
| GAP-1374 | Couleur des liens du message | Accent du thème (`--color-action`), 1,5:1 en clair à la teinte par défaut | `style-liste-light.css:339-341, 631-633` @ `87fe0d1c` | Accent éclairci ou assombri jusqu'à 4,5:1 sur toutes les surfaces ; l'accent reste pour les remplissages | #1374 | UX change | new UX: spec | b |
```

**Adversarial review (Opus 5.5, mac/mac-mbp-r1389, head da3c0349)**: REQUEST CHANGES

Agent: mac/mac-mbp-r1389 (Opus 5.5)

1. **Medium**: PR body, "Legacy look decision" and "no `### Ledger`". The claim that legacy body links were WebKit's default blue is wrong. At `87fe0d1c` the reader page loads `style-liste-light.css` (`Classes/ObjCTopicHTMLRenderer.m:28`). That file has `.message .content .right a { color:var(--color-action) }` (`SuperHFRplus/Assets/HTML/style-liste-light.css:339-341`), and the message body sits in `div.content > div.right` (`templatev2.htm:10-12`). `--color-action` is `ThemeColors.tintColor(theme)` (`HFRswift/Swift/MessagesView.swift:2833,2841`), which is `actionTintColorForLegacyThemeValue`, the hue-slider accent (`Classes/ThemeColors.m:618-619`). The `[code]` keyword is the accent too (`.olcode .span`, `style-liste-light.css:631-633`). So legacy draws body links in the accent at 1.5:1, the same as SwiftHFR before this PR. This PR deliberately changes legacy behaviour, so it owes a `### Ledger` section (a `changelog` entry for the legacy contrast bug it fixes and a `gap-new` row: links and the code keyword in an accent-derived colour, #1374), per AGENTS.md §8. The operator's look decision also rests on this premise: correct the paragraph.
2. **Low**: `reader.css:249` still says the keyword colour is "the action colour" (`LinkItem.m:265`). It is `--link` now: say so in the comment.
3. **Detail (same class, out of scope)**: the dark preview in « Thème » draws "Une citation" in `nightAccent` (`ThemeSettingsView.swift:172-173`), which is 2.24:1 at 240°. This is accent-coloured text outside the reader: open an issue rather than fixing it here.

Checked and found sound: the bisection terminates (24 steps, and the accent is returned when it already passes). Mixing toward black or white in sRGB keeps HSB hue exactly. The pass set is an interval because every surface is lighter (light) or darker (dark) than the target. The model's surfaces match `reader.css` (`--text`, `--love`, `--modo`, the 15 % header and own-message tint, nesting, and the continuation fade composited over the page). `a` also covers visited links. `b.s1 a` and the bubble or video pill keep their own colours. Noël soft recomputes from the red accent. Gallery themes keep `--link` from their checked `link` token, which THEMES.md §3 already checks on code.

**Verified**: worktree at da3c0349; read the diff, #1374, `reader.css`, `ThemeAppearance*`, `ThemeSettingsView`; `git show`/`git grep` at `87fe0d1c` (light, dark and OLED CSS, templates, `ThemeColors.m`, `MessagesView.swift`); `pre-commit run` on the touched files (passed); manual SwiftLint check (no line over 140, files 65 and 159 lines, at most 2 parameters, 2-tuples). Hosted suites **not run**: load average stayed at about 750 (the limit is 8), so I took no simulator slot. I did not reproduce the red-without-change run; the CI macOS job has to stand in.

**mac/mac-mbp**: CI fix, head below.

`ReaderThemeTests` (first, live, light, restored) read the computed colour of a link and compared it with the accent; since #1374 a link paints `--link`, the derived colour. Not a regression: the live theme change and the Legacy restore both update `--link` (the tests now pass waiting on the derived value). They now expect `ThemeAppearance.linkColor(dark:).cssRGB` of the appearance under test (the gallery-theme assertion, `#8CC8FF`, is unchanged). Tests that read `--action` directly (fills, tints, the plus button) are unaffected.

**Adversarial review (Opus 5.5, mac/mac-mbp-r1389, head ef6cb034)**: APPROVE

Agent: mac/mac-mbp-r1389 (Opus 5.5)

Round 3, the delta d31abe6f..ef6cb034 (`ReaderThemeTests.swift` only).

The new expectation is right, and each test would still catch the failure it is there for:
- **Exact strings.** The link variables are sent as `cssRGB`, which rounds to integer channels (`ThemeAppearance.swift:296-299`). A string comparison with `getComputedStyle(a).color` is therefore exact and not flaky.
- **Light and dark first theme.** `theLightVariantGetsTheDayAccentsLink` and the first step of the dark test use pure red and pure blue accents. Both fail 4.7:1 on their page (red 4.0 on white, blue 2.4 on black at 0 % brightness), so `linkColor` differs from the accent. If `--app-link-*` were no longer sent, `--link` would fall back to `--action` and both tests would fail.
- **Live change.** The colour expected after the change (night red at 100 %) differs from the first one (night blue at 0 %). If a live change stopped updating `--app-link-dark`, the page would keep the first link and the test would fail.
- **Legacy restore.** It expects `standard.linkColor(dark: true)`, which differs from the gallery theme's `rgb(140, 200, 255)` shown just before. A restore that leaves the theme's `--link` in place fails. This step alone does not tell the derived link from the raw accent (they may be close for the standard accent); the two tests above cover that.

No other test asserts a link's colour against the raw accent. `ThemeAppearanceTests:30-31, 53-54, 68` check `--app-action-*` variables, which this PR leaves unchanged. `ReaderWebSecurityTests:97` checks an author's inline colour. `VisibilityWebTests` reads borders and tints, not link text. `ReaderVideoLinkTests` has no colour assertion.

The expectation comes from the production `linkColor`. That is fine for a plumbing test: whether the colour reaches 4.5:1 is checked independently on rendered colours by `ReaderLinkContrastWebTests`.

**Verified**: `git diff d31abe6f ef6cb034`; read the probes (`ReaderThemeTests.swift:10-33`); `git grep` at ef6cb034 for colour assertions on links and accents across `App/SwiftHFRTests`; hand-computed the contrast of the test accents. I ran nothing on a simulator (the Mac is busy). The author's run (186 tests in 18 suites) and the CI macOS run once the PR is ready stand in for the suites.
